nodes.label: Final Recap Experience
nodes.rationale: Played after all 3 curriculum terms, mostly self-directed over the holidays. Must touch everything taught across the year in one 20-30 min sitting, so it is ordered for narrative pacing rather than Term 1-2-3 calendar order.

nodes.label: One Game, One App, One Entry Point
nodes.rationale: Corrected from an earlier two-separate-apps decision. Content is fully separate per band (different scenarios, different mechanics for 2 of 5 realms) but delivered as a single product; the separation lives in content data and component logic, not app architecture.
nodes.norm_label: one game, one app, one entry point

nodes.label: P1-P3 / P4-P6 Band Split
nodes.rationale: The Atlas Gate asks the student which band they are in; every downstream screen reads content from the schema using that value (band: 'lower' | 'higher').

nodes.label: Term 1 - Healthy Digital Habits
nodes.rationale: Four core habits: Set Boundaries Online, Think Before You Act, Report Inappropriate Content, Engage and Support. Written as one unified curriculum for all of P1-P6, with no band split.

nodes.label: Term 2 - Recess Activities
nodes.rationale: Reinforcement plus pledge: Be Safe / Be Kind / Be Smart Online, Balance is Key, When Things Go Wrong. Also unified across P1-P6.

nodes.label: STOP & CHECK Method (P1-P3)
nodes.rationale: STOP - pause; CHECK - ask a trusted adult or check another source. The lower band's media-literacy framework for Fable Falls.

nodes.label: S.U.R.E. Framework (P4-P6)
nodes.rationale: Source / Understand / Research / Evaluate. The higher band's media-literacy framework for Fable Falls.

nodes.label: Cyber Defender Quest
nodes.rationale: Confirmed 18 Aug 2026 as the capstone activity name (not 'Cyber Detective Quest' as earlier drafts suggested); built as the P4-P6 Fable Falls mini-game's title.

nodes.label: Fable Falls Realm
nodes.rationale: The fifth realm, covering fake news and altered images. Name resolved 18 Aug 2026 and shipped the same day by working around the unsourced official content rather than waiting on it. Carries a 5th accent colour (--sage) and stamp icon (eye).

nodes.label: The Echo
nodes.rationale: Fable Falls' guide character - repeats whatever it hears without checking it, the personification of a rumour rather than a villain, consistent with the cast's no-villain rule.

nodes.label: Digital Footprint / Positive Digital Trail
nodes.rationale: Top-priority content gap: appears in both Term 1 (Think Before You Act) and Term 2 (Be Smart Online), so two independent source mentions. Fixed as a decision beat inside Bully Bog alongside the kindness choice, since the curriculum pairs 'respectful' and 'positive trail' in one sentence.

nodes.label: Report & Block Resolution Option
nodes.rationale: Given a reusable resolution option at the redirect moment in every realm rather than a dedicated realm, because the curriculum itself always pairs it with another habit and never treats it standalone.

nodes.label: Engage and Support
nodes.rationale: A named Term 1 habit with no clear home; addressed by giving Comet an explicit 'who would you tell?' prompt at Bully Bog's bystander moment, reinforcing that seeking help is itself a habit, not just a fallback.

nodes.label: Respect Others' Work (Plagiarism / IP)
nodes.rationale: Smallest gap - one bullet under Be Smart Online. Planned to fold into Fable Falls' Understand/Research step as a light touch, but the shipped content does not yet touch it; still the lowest-priority gap.

nodes.label: 3 Tips to CHECK (Unsourced SLS Content)
nodes.rationale: A missing source-material gap rather than a design gap - it lives in the SLS lesson package, not the Overview Plan. Worked around with general media-literacy signals (source credibility, cross-checking, does-it-add-up reasoning), flagged in realms.js as a placeholder pending swap-in. Low risk either way since it is just data.

nodes.label: Realm Plan by Band
nodes.rationale: Maps each of the five realms to a P1-P3 and a P4-P6 mechanic and framing, plus Report & Block as a universal addition wherever a redirect moment happens.

nodes.label: Suggested Play Order per Band
nodes.rationale: Open with each band's own signature classroom scenario so the recap lands as 'remember this?', middle realms in either order, Fake News last as a synthesis challenge drawing on judgement built earlier, then the Pledge. Free exploration stays; this is a default, not a gate.

nodes.label: Band Differentiation as Design Enrichment
nodes.rationale: Harder mechanics, more nuanced scenarios and different stakes for P4-P6 are the team's own design extension, not curriculum-mandated - Terms 1 and 2 are one-size-fits-all and only Term 3 splits by band. The Luke vs Sam & Tom split began as a suggestion in the Lesson Plan doc and hardened only in later slide decks. Disclosed as a design choice and confirmed age-appropriate by the school contact.

nodes.label: P4-5 vs P4-6 Resolution
nodes.rationale: The source doc writes the S.U.R.E. band as '(P4-5)' consistently in all three places it appears. Decision 18 Aug 2026: treat P4-5 as P4-6, so all of P4-P6 gets S.U.R.E. with no special-casing P6 out.

nodes.label: Fifth Traveler's Pledge Line
nodes.rationale: 'I'll stop and check before I believe or share.' - the Fable Falls line, live in the certificate as of 18 Aug 2026 now that activePledge() no longer filters it out. Wording sign-off remains informally open.

nodes.label: Phase 0 - Foundation
nodes.rationale: Shared design system plus content schema: shared-component audit, 5-realm per-band schema, band-select in the Atlas Gate, Phaser as a scoped lazy dependency, placeholder asset pipeline. Programmer half done.

nodes.label: Phase 1 - Content Authoring
nodes.rationale: Realm content data per band per realm for all 5 realms, the Report & Block component, Bully Bog's digital-footprint and 'who would you tell' beats, the 5th pledge line, and the hardcoded-realm-count audit. Done.

nodes.label: Phase 3 - Backgrounds
nodes.rationale: Scaling the existing 9 backgrounds. Realistic total is ~13-14 pieces, not 18 - it is one shared world regardless of band, plus the Traveler's Room as an unplanned 10th location.

nodes.label: Asset Pipeline (Placeholders & Specs)
nodes.rationale: Exists so the programmer is not blocked waiting on final art and the designer is not guessing at dimensions. Placeholders and final art use the exact same file path, so swapping is a file replacement rather than a code change.

nodes.label: ART_MANIFEST Texture Declaration
nodes.rationale: Chosen over flat-colour placeholder image files because it hands the designer a named, measured shopping list (15 textures with filenames, frame sizes and counts, plus ART_ANIMS) instead of rectangles to reverse-engineer, and keeps the scene code art-agnostic. Its measured sizes supersede the spec table's guessed 64x64, which was invented before the 1120x280 level existed.

nodes.label: Skin-Based Art Swap-In (SKINS / ACTIVE_SKIN)
nodes.rationale: A skin declares only the textures it actually replaces and carries its own frame sizes, animation frame lists and player hitbox, so a partial art delivery still runs and a missing or corrupt file falls back silently to the procedural version instead of crashing.

nodes.label: Brackeys CC0 Placeholder Skin
nodes.rationale: ACTIVE_SKIN = 'brackeys' maps the traveler to knight.png and the hacker to slime_purple.png. Deliberately pixel art, not the game's flat vector style - it proves the swap path works but must be replaced.

nodes.label: No Godot - Stay on React/Vite
nodes.rationale: The Godot port was dropped with no code written against it. A single web codebase avoids a second toolchain and keeps the zero-install browser deployment; a Godot HTML5 export would add a WASM runtime, the wrong trade for load time on older school devices.

nodes.label: Phaser Scoped to Two Mechanics, Lazy-Loaded
nodes.rationale: Phaser is used only for the Platformer and stepping-stone run, for its physics/animation tooling; every other mechanic stays plain React because the existing pattern already works. It loads only when a P4-P6 player enters Passworld or Privacy Peaks, so the hub, the other realms and the whole P1-P3 path never pay for it (~1.48MB chunk vs a ~248KB main bundle).
nodes.norm_label: phaser scoped to two mechanics, lazy-loaded

nodes.label: PhaserMiniGame Wrapper
nodes.rationale: Mounts and unmounts a Phaser canvas inside a React container and cleans up on unmount. Extended to accept a (Phaser) => config factory, because a Scene class must extend Phaser.Scene and cannot be defined until the dynamic import resolves.

nodes.label: Platformer Mechanic (Guard the Vault: Level Up)
nodes.rationale: Passworld P4-P6, reworked into one continuous 3144px scrollable Phaser level in five movements so story, the Sam & Tom decision and the vault challenge all live inside the scene, gated by a portcullis rather than a DOM panel. Six characters to collect because a strong password is a long one; all 19 jumps verified against the physics rather than eyeballed; guards snapped onto their platforms with 190px ledges and a 440px/s knockback.
nodes.norm_label: platformer mechanic (guard the vault: level up)

nodes.label: Stepping-Stone Decision Run
nodes.rationale: Privacy Peaks P4-P6. Six stones presented one at a time with Step-on-it/Skip-it; decision logic stays in React (same pattern as MiniGameSpot) and Phaser is purely the visual run of stones, fog and the Traveler hop. Still has no ART_MANIFEST/skin treatment.

nodes.label: Detective/Compare Mechanic (MiniGameCompare)
nodes.rationale: Unblocked by dropping the assumption that 'Compare' means two photographs - the comparison that carries a media-literacy lesson is the trusted original against the version going around, which is text and chrome, so it needed no art and was never actually blocked. One component serves both bands via a framework field ('stopcheck' for P1-P3, 'sure' for P4-P6); controls are Sort's and Spot's, and only an exact match completes it. Replaced the Spot/Sort stand-ins in Fable Falls.

nodes.label: A Mini-Game Must Not Be Passable Without Judgement
nodes.rationale: An audit found four of five mini-games could be finished without deciding anything, so they looked like they taught judgement while rewarding exhaustive clicking - exactly the habit these lessons exist to counter. All four now require the judgement to be right, with free retries and no fail state: the fix is never punishment, it is removing the path that skipped the thinking. Balance Bay is deliberately excepted because it is a values exercise with no correct answer, so gating it would misrepresent what it teaches.
nodes.norm_label: a mini-game must not be passable without judgement

nodes.label: Vault Door Judgement Gate
nodes.rationale: Everything collected goes into a bag, weak pieces included, and a locked vault door on the final platform asks which of them belong in a strong password. Two gates: it refuses outright if the strong pieces are not all there, and otherwise the player must pick them out from the decoys they also carried up. Decoys had to become collectable for this to mean anything.

nodes.label: Removed Visual Tells
nodes.rationale: Five tells gave the answer away before the student read a word: closed vs open padlocks on tile art, gold gloss and sparkles on decoys, real tiles hovering while decoys glinted, a HUD reading 'n of 6 strong', and a strength meter that filled only on real pickups and ran red-to-teal. Two had been explicitly requested by the designer brief, now corrected there. One uniform collectible design is a hard constraint, not a preference.

nodes.label: Input Scope: Keyboard + Mouse Only
nodes.rationale: Decided 19 Aug 2026. Touch/tablet parity is explicitly not a goal; the on-screen d-pad, tap-to-move, drag-to-steer and 48px tap-target items were dropped rather than deferred. This closes the former keyboard-only 'blocker' - WASD/arrows to walk and Space/Enter to interact are the intended primary input, not a regression.

nodes.label: Band Select in the Atlas Gate
nodes.rationale: A routing/state decision inside the existing gate flow, not a second app shell. Restaged 18-19 Aug 2026 as a panel over the Traveler's Room rather than a bare card screen, so what needs designing is the panel chrome, not a full screen.
nodes.norm_label: band select in the atlas gate

nodes.label: The Traveler's Room Prologue
nodes.rationale: The game opens in the Traveler's bedroom instead of a card screen: walk to a glowing diary, Comet unfolds out of it, naming and band-select run as a panel over the room, then the door leads out to the Atlas. Built on the existing World/useWalker layer so it inherited hotspots, objectives and pausing for free. Ships third-party pixel art in an otherwise flat-vector game - a style call nobody has made yet, on the first screen every student sees.

nodes.label: Hub Order Doc Disagreement
nodes.rationale: HUB_ORDER is still keyed by band but both keys point at one array taken from storyline.md's Story Arc Overview, while Improvement Plan section 4 still specifies two different per-band orders. Reinstating a split is a one-line change; the open decision is which doc wins.

nodes.label: Session Persistence (localStorage)
nodes.rationale: Not a gap - travelerName, band, realmProgress and pledgeSigned have persisted to localStorage under 'cyber-wellness-quest/v1' since before this project's phases began, so the self-directed-over-the-holidays scenario is already covered.

nodes.label: ReportBlock Component
nodes.rationale: The reusable Report & Block resolution, wired into the redirect moment in every realm.

nodes.label: Per-Band Realm Content Schema
nodes.rationale: realms.js restructured to bands: { lower, higher } per realm with getBandView() resolution and a null-band fallback to lower, plus ACTIVE_REALMS filtering disabled realms so every consumer reads the realm count from the schema instead of hardcoding four. Band objects swap wholesale rather than per-field, so a band needing its own extraBeats carries them itself.

nodes.label: Branching Atlas Map
nodes.rationale: The hub's single winding stream became 5 branches fanning out from the Gate, one per realm, so any hub art must be drawn against the new layout. The Atlas also now remembers where the Traveler left the boat via atlasPos rather than returning them to the Gate.

nodes.label: Fixed Viewport, No Page Scrolling
nodes.rationale: A 2:1 scene box wide enough to play is half the viewport tall on its own, so stacking it in one column made every screen scroll. Screens with content below the box now use a two-column stage that restacks under 900px, and the box takes its height from its container and derives width via aspect-ratio - sizing it as a share of the viewport cannot work because the chrome above it differs per screen.

nodes.label: Latin-Only Font Subsets
nodes.rationale: The bare @fontsource weight entrypoints shipped devanagari, vietnamese and cyrillic subsets - 76% of a 1023KB payload for a game with no text in those scripts. unicode-range meant browsers never downloaded them, so this is a deploy-size win rather than a first-paint one, but it matters for the older-school-devices constraint.

nodes.label: Reduced-Motion Coverage Gap
nodes.rationale: The prefers-reduced-motion block only blankets CSS animation and transition; the Phaser tweens (guard patrols, tile hover, vault door, win sequence) and the rAF walker are JS-driven and ignore it entirely.

nodes.label: Walkable Realm Scene
nodes.rationale: Each realm is a 2D scene walked with arrow keys/WASD, interacted with via Space/Enter at a pin. Each step (story, decision, mini-game, rule) moves the pin, and the scene itself changes once the safe choice is made - the vault opens, the fog lifts, the water clears, the tide goes out.

nodes.label: Ground Rule: scene_y = world_y x 2.8
nodes.rationale: Scene art (560x280 viewBox in RealmArt.jsx) and the walkable band (0-100 world units in data/realms.js) live in two coordinate systems and nothing enforces that they agree. Two rules follow: solid ground must be drawn across the entire walkable band in both moods, and nothing solid may float above the band, because World.jsx draws the Traveler over the scene with no depth sorting. Breaking either has already produced real bugs - a campfire burning on open water, a Traveler walking across a bog.

nodes.label: No Fail State, Warm Redirect
nodes.rationale: Nothing can be failed. Picking the unsafe option gets a warm redirect from Comet and hands the decision straight back - no dead end, no timer, and no score shown to the player.

nodes.label: Step Panel Portal to Body
nodes.rationale: The step panel renders through a portal to <body> because .fold animates a perspective()/rotateY() transform, which makes it a containing block - a position:fixed scrim inside it would resolve against the realm card instead of the viewport. Panel action rows are sticky to the bottom, because a long story beat can otherwise push the only way forward below the fold and a child who cannot see the button is simply stuck.

nodes.label: Known Deviations from the Design Docs
nodes.rationale: Three deliberate calls logged so docs and build do not quietly drift: a walkable world instead of design.md section 5's point-and-click cards; a real Vite app with localStorage persistence instead of section 9's single-file artifact; and a third mini-game component, because section 5's own 'Balance the Day' is a scale rather than two bins - it reuses Sort's exact click-to-place controls so there is no new control to learn.
nodes.norm_label: known deviations from the design docs

nodes.label: Asset Folder & Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: shared/ for art used by both bands within the one app, p4-6-only/ for the platformer and stepping-stone sprite sheets, fablefalls-detective/ for per-band clue assets. Includes the-echo.svg and stamp-eye.svg for the fifth realm.

nodes.label: Asset Specs Table
nodes.rationale: Proposed defaults to confirm against live repo constants, then lock. Scene backgrounds 560x280 SVG matching the scene_y = world_y x 2.8 convention; platformer frames proposed at 64x64 - a guess the Milestones doc later supersedes with manifest-measured sizes; stepping-stone sprites 128x128 because they are tap targets, not run-cycle frames; detective clue assets stay SVG because that mechanic is plain React, not Phaser.

nodes.label: The Atlas Concept
nodes.rationale: The internet reframed as a living map made of realms the player travels through with a guide. Each realm teaches one cyber wellness topic through a story beat, a branching decision, and a small hands-on mini-game.

nodes.label: Field-Journal / Passport Metaphor
nodes.rationale: Grounds the whole product: the player is a Traveler filling in a journal, and every earned badge is a physical-feeling ink stamp rather than a digital trophy icon. This gives the internet the sense of a place worth exploring thoughtfully - like a nature reserve visited with a guide and a notebook - rather than a void to fear or a screen to be babysat through.

nodes.label: Avoided Tropes (Neon Cyberspace, Warm Cream)
nodes.rationale: Neon-cyberspace-on-black reads as scary or hacker-coded, working against the message that the internet is a place kids can explore safely. The generic warm-cream-and-serif 'AI design' default flattens personality and does not fit an energetic kids' product.

nodes.label: Design Token System
nodes.rationale: paper/ink/ink-soft plus one accent per realm (gold, teal, coral, periwinkle). Each realm accent is used only inside that realm's screens and its stamp, and shared UI stays ink/paper, so the realm colours read as distinct regions of the map rather than a rainbow UI. Type splits into display, body at 18-20px, and a monospace stamp/label face that must not leak into body copy.

nodes.label: The Ink Stamp Badge
nodes.rationale: The signature element: a circular, slightly irregular-edged stamp in the realm accent with a simple icon and a monospace label, landing at a randomized -6 to 6 degree rotation so the journal page feels hand-stamped rather than templated. Everything else in the UI stays quiet so it does not compete.

nodes.label: Screen Flow
nodes.rationale: Atlas Gate to the hub, then five realms each running story to choice to mini-game to stamp and back to the hub, with the finale unlocking once every stamp is earned. Every realm branches out from the Gate and is reachable from the start - free exploration in any order; the storyline.md table order is only the suggested pacing shown in the realm-strip list.

nodes.label: Sort Mechanic
nodes.rationale: Drag items into two labeled bins, reused across Passworld, Bully Bog and Balance Bay with different content so kids do not have to learn new controls each time. Now gated by the judgement rule - it used to file every card into its correct bin whichever one the player picked.

nodes.label: Spot Mechanic
nodes.rationale: Click the flagged items within a scene or message, used in Privacy Peaks. Now gated by the judgement rule - it used to reveal whether a message was a real problem the instant it was clicked, so clicking everything scored full marks.

nodes.label: Balance the Day Mechanic
nodes.rationale: Daily activity tiles placed on a scale until it settles level. There is no single correct split - extreme all-or-nothing arrangements tip it hard, teaching balance rather than a strict number. Its own component rather than a Sort variant, but reusing Sort's exact click-to-place controls. Deliberately exempt from the judgement rule because it is a values exercise, not a right/wrong one.

nodes.label: Component Inventory
nodes.rationale: AtlasMap, RealmScreen, DialogueCard, ChoiceCard, MiniGameSort, MiniGameSpot, StampBadge, JournalProgress, CertificateScreen - each written generic, taking items/scene config/realm data as props.

nodes.label: State & Data Model
nodes.rationale: travelerName, currentScreen, and a realmProgress map of { storyDone, choiceMade, gameScore, stamped } per realm. Originally in-memory only because artifacts cannot use browser storage; persistence was flagged as the follow-up once the base game existed, and is now localStorage-backed.

nodes.label: Accessibility & Kid-Safety UX Notes
nodes.rationale: Generous focusable click targets; no timers, fail states or score pressure, with free retries; a text-equivalent instruction line on every mini-game; colour never the only signal for safe/unsafe; and no real personal data requested beyond an in-session first name. Input scope decided 19 Aug 2026 as keyboard + mouse only, so there are no touch-specific controls to build or maintain.

nodes.label: Technical Constraints
nodes.rationale: Originally a single-file React artifact: Tailwind core utilities only, no localStorage, lucide-react icons, no framer-motion, and no external image assets - all character and scene art built from SVG shapes, consistent with the flat vector direction. The shipped build deviates on the artifact and storage points.

nodes.label: Scene Construction Rules
nodes.rationale: Added once the realms became walkable, which introduced a constraint the card design never had: the art has to agree with the ground the player can stand on. Solid ground across the whole band in both moods, and nothing solid floating above the band since there is no depth sorting. Breaking these is not a subtle rendering nit - it reads immediately as broken to a child. Already caught: a bonfire and friends burning on open water, a bog with no bank, a Keeper hovering twenty units above the ground.

nodes.label: Motion & Animation Direction
nodes.rationale: Revised 18 Aug 2026 - the original 'exactly two moments' budget made the game read as static rather than calm, especially the Phaser mini-games. The stamp thunk and page-fold stay the biggest beats, but every interaction now gets real felt feedback: buttons press, safe choices settle in with a pop, the interact pin invites more visibly, and Phaser pickups get a collect animation instead of just disappearing. Punchier, not louder.

nodes.label: The Atlas
nodes.rationale: A living map of the internet made of realms, drawn by an old glowing journal that fills itself in when opened. The journal is the player's passport.

nodes.label: The Traveler
nodes.rationale: The player. Name entered at the start and used throughout. No fixed appearance is described in text, so the art can keep the avatar simple, abstract and inclusive.

nodes.label: Comet
nodes.rationale: The guide: a paper-airplane spirit who knows every realm and its tricks. Warm, a little playful, never lectures - Comet asks questions more than it gives answers and treats mistakes as normal parts of exploring. Catchphrase opening each realm: 'Every good traveler carries two things: curiosity, and a second thought.'

nodes.label: Keeper Vex
nodes.rationale: Passworld's guardian - good-natured but overly chatty, and thinks every question is fine to ask a stranger. Not a villain; he laughs, embarrassed, when the player declines.

nodes.label: The Fog
nodes.rationale: Privacy Peaks' presence - not a villain, just mist that hides who is really on the other side of a message. Different fog-shapes speak with different scam tactics.

nodes.label: Pockets the Frog
nodes.rationale: A shy bog-dweller who gets a mean comment posted about their singing. Central to Bully Bog's 'stand up, don't join in' lesson.

nodes.label: The Glimmer
nodes.rationale: Balance Bay's shimmering tide-spirit that makes 'just five more minutes' feel like no time has passed at all. Not evil, just very good at being fun.

nodes.label: Atlas Gate (Prologue)
nodes.rationale: Comet unfolds from the journal's last page, the player enters their name and receives the passport with empty stamp circles, and Comet gives the one rule that threads through every realm before the Atlas hub opens.

nodes.label: Passworld
nodes.rationale: A walled kingdom of vault doors. Teaches passwords and personal info via Keeper Vex asking for everything, a decision, and the 'Guard the Vault' sort into Keep It Locked vs Safe to Share. Stamp: the Key.

nodes.label: Privacy Peaks
nodes.rationale: Misty mountain lookouts where visibility is low - that is the point. Teaches strangers and scams via a prize-scam message from the Fog and 'Clear the Fog', clicking the red-flag phrases. Stamp: the Compass.

nodes.label: Bully Bog
nodes.rationale: A swampy bog whose murky water reflects whatever is posted about its residents. Teaches cyberbullying and kindness via Pockets' mean comment and 'Clear the Water', sorting comments into Send It vs Leave It. Comet states the wider rule regardless of path taken: if it is ever about you, do not respond to be mean back - save it and show a trusted adult. Stamp: the Heart.

nodes.label: Balance Bay
nodes.rationale: A beach at dusk with an unusually high tide - the Glimmer's doing - and friends waiting by a distant bonfire. Teaches screen-time balance; the unsafe choice does not block progress, it just starts the mini-game with the scale already tipped. Stamp: the Sun.

nodes.label: The Traveler's Pledge
nodes.rationale: One line per realm, written in the child's own future voice rather than as rules handed down, and 'signed' by the child on the certificate.

nodes.label: Wise Traveler Certificate
nodes.rationale: The finale, triggered by returning to the Atlas Gate with every stamp earned: the Traveler's name, the stamps in a row, and the pledge. Ends with Comet folding back into the journal, leaving the door open for replay.

nodes.label: No Fear-Based Framing
nodes.rationale: Nothing is a monster or a villain; every wrong choice is a misunderstanding to retry, not a danger the child narrowly escaped. This is why Vex, the Fog and the Glimmer are all sympathetic rather than threats.
